_readme: Eval set for the Star Health Assure policy wording PDF (20 pages). Page numbers in 'source' are viewer page numbers (1-based); the app's citations are PyMuPDF indices (0-based). answerable=false means the correct behaviour is a refusal.

items.question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
items.ground_truth: The waiting period for pre-existing diseases depends on the policy term: 36 months for 1-year and 2-year policy terms, and 30 months for a 3-year policy term.

items.question: What is the room rent limit per day?
items.ground_truth: It depends on the sum insured. For a sum insured of Rs 5 lakh the limit is up to 1% of the sum insured per day (Rs 5,000 per day). For Rs 10 lakh, 15 lakh, 20 lakh and 25 lakh it is any room except Suite or a higher category. For Rs 50 lakh, 75 lakh, 1 crore and 2 crore it is any room with no room category restriction.
items.source: Pages 6, 19 (room rent criteria table; Schedule of Benefits row 1)

items.question: Is maternity covered? What is the sub-limit?
items.ground_truth: Yes. Maternity (delivery expenses) is covered, including normal delivery, caesarean section, and pre-natal and post-natal expenses. The sub-limit is up to 10% of the sum insured for each delivery.

items.question: What are the exclusions?
items.ground_truth: The main exclusions include pre-existing diseases, specified diseases and procedures excluded for the first 24 months unless caused by an accident (for example cataract, ENT diseases, thyroid disorders, hernia, gallstones, kidney stones, joint replacement, spinal disorders, gynaecological conditions, prostate diseases, haemorrhoids), the 30-day waiting period, hospital admission primarily for investigation or evaluation, rest cure, rehabilitation and respite care, obesity or weight-control treatment, cosmetic or plastic surgery unless medically necessary due to accident, burns or illness, hazardous or adventure sports injuries, breach of law, treatment outside India, war or nuclear risks, unproven treatments, and certain non-medical expenses.

items.question: What are the sum insured options available?
items.ground_truth: The sum insured options are Rs 5 lakh, 10 lakh, 15 lakh, 20 lakh, 25 lakh, 50 lakh, 75 lakh, 1 crore and 2 crore.
items.source: Pages 6, 7, 19, 20 (full list appears in the room rent and health check-up tables on p6, the sub-limit tables on p7, and the Schedule of Benefits header on p19-20)

items.question: What is the ICU charge limit?
items.ground_truth: ICU and operation theatre charges are payable at actuals for every sum insured, so there is no separate ICU limit.

items.question: Are AYUSH treatments covered?
items.ground_truth: Yes. AYUSH treatments are covered under the policy.

items.question: What is the free look period?
items.ground_truth: The free look period is 15 days from the date of receipt of the policy document. It applies only to new individual health insurance policies, not to renewals, porting or migration. During this period the insured can review the terms and return the policy if they are not acceptable.

items.question: Is there coverage for day care procedures?
items.ground_truth: Yes. All day care treatments are covered, meaning medical or surgical procedures that do not require 24-hour hospitalisation because of advances in medical technology. Certain modern treatments are covered whether done as an in-patient or as day care in a hospital, subject to the policy terms.

items.question: What happens if I miss a premium payment?
items.ground_truth: For renewal premium there is a 30-day grace period to renew and keep continuity benefits, but there is no coverage during the grace period. For instalment premium (half-yearly or quarterly) there is a 7-day grace period; if the premium is not paid within it the policy is cancelled, and there is no coverage from the due date until the premium is received.

items.question: Is treatment for asthma included in the insurance?
items.ground_truth: Chronic Severe Refractory Asthma is specifically covered. In-patient hospitalization, day care, home care and out-patient expenses for treatment by Advanced Medicine are payable up to 10% of the sum insured, not exceeding Rs 5 lakhs per policy period, when recommended by the treating medical practitioner (pulmonologist).

items.question: Is treatment for a new born baby covered?
items.ground_truth: Yes. Hospitalization expenses of a new born baby are covered from day 1 of birth until the expiry of the policy, up to Rs 2,00,000 per policy period for sums insured of Rs 5 lakh to 25 lakh and Rs 4,00,000 for Rs 50 lakh to 2 crore. The cover is available only if a Delivery Expenses claim is paid under this policy or the mother has been covered under this policy for a continuous 12 months without a break, and the birth must be intimated to the company. These limits do not apply to treatment of congenital internal diseases or defects of the new born. From the following years the baby is covered up to the sum insured if the policyholder opts for new born cover and pays the premium.

items.question: What is the waiting period for cataract surgery?
items.ground_truth: A waiting period of 24 months of continuous coverage from the date of inception of the first policy applies to cataract, which is in the list of specified diseases and procedures (Code Excl 02). It does not apply to claims arising from an accident. The waiting period is reduced by prior continuous coverage under IRDAI portability norms, and applies afresh to the extent of any increase in sum insured.

items.question: What is the initial waiting period after the policy starts?
items.ground_truth: The initial waiting period is 30 days from the first policy commencement date. Claims arising from an accident are excluded from this waiting period, provided they are otherwise covered. It does not apply if the insured person has continuous coverage of more than twelve months.

items.question: How many days of pre-hospitalisation and post-hospitalisation expenses are covered?
items.ground_truth: 60 days of pre-hospitalisation expenses and 180 days of post-hospitalisation expenses are covered.

items.question: Is ambulance cover included, and what is the limit?
items.ground_truth: Yes. Emergency road ambulance expenses are covered at actuals, subject to an admissible hospitalization claim. Air ambulance expenses are covered up to 10% of the sum insured per policy year, subject to conditions.

items.question: How soon must a claim be intimated to the insurer?
items.ground_truth: The insurer must be notified within 24 hours of the occurrence of the event. The insurer may relax this time limit depending on the merits of the case.

items.question: Is there a co-payment under this policy?
items.ground_truth: Yes. A 10% co-payment applies to every claim, for fresh as well as renewal policies, for insured persons whose age at entry was 61 years or above.

items.question: Does the policy offer a cumulative bonus, and how much?
items.ground_truth: Yes. A cumulative bonus of 25% of the sum insured for each claim-free year, up to a maximum of 100% of the sum insured, is provided.

items.question: Is there a health check-up benefit?
items.ground_truth: Yes. Health Checkup Assure covers health check-up expenses every policy year, irrespective of claims, up to limits that depend on the sum insured and on whether the policy is individual or floater (for example Rs 1,500 individual and Rs 2,500 floater at a sum insured of Rs 5 lakh).

items.question: Are organ donor expenses covered?
items.ground_truth: Yes. In-patient hospitalization expenses of the donor for organ transplantation to an insured recipient are covered, provided the transplant claim is payable, including donor expenses for complications needing redo surgery or ICU admission. The donor coverage is over and above the limit of coverage and up to the sum insured.

items.question: Can I cancel the policy mid-term, and is there a refund?
items.ground_truth: Yes. The policyholder may cancel the policy by giving 15 days' written notice, and the insurer refunds premium for the unexpired period according to the cancellation table. No refund is made if a claim has been admitted or lodged or any benefit has been availed.

items.question: Does the policy cover dental treatment?
items.ground_truth: The Customer Information Sheet lists corrective and cosmetic dental surgeries among the major exclusions. The policy wording does not otherwise state whether other dental treatment is covered.

items.question: What is the cashless claim procedure?
items.ground_truth: Cashless treatment is available only at network hospitals. The insured calls the insurer's help-line and informs the ID number, produces the insurer's ID card at the hospital helpdesk, and completes the pre-authorisation form there. The treating doctor fills in the treatment details and the hospital fills in the expected cost, and the form is submitted to the insurer, who may ask for more documents and then approves or rejects the request. In an emergency hospitalization the insurer must be informed within 24 hours.

items.question: What is the maximum entry age for the policy?
items.ground_truth: The policy does not mention a maximum entry age.
